current.text: He is playing in preseason and looks okay. He is expected to be available on opening night after ankle surgery.
Experts still see a high injury risk and expect him to get some days off.
He is in the projected Memphis starting five at center.
Experts expect about 25 to 28 minutes a night, not 30 or more. Memphis wants to manage his large frame, and Isaiah Stewart and Quinten Post should take the extra center minutes.
Coach Tuomas Iisalo plays at a very high pace, uses short stints, keeps minutes down and runs an 11 or 12 man rotation.
One expert projects about 65 games, partly because Edey is thinking about his contract extension.
In his 11 games last season he ranked around 60th to 70th per game in about 26 minutes. One expert called him the best second-year player per game.
Experts see top-50 upside if he stays healthy, and Lloyd calls him a league winner. At 30 minutes a night he could be a top-30 to top-40 player. One expert says he is a top-60 player at worst.
Experts take him around picks 60 to 70 in recent mock drafts. One goes as early as round 5.
Experts call his ESPN rank and ADP (113 to 124) great value, a gap of 40 to 50 spots. At a Yahoo ADP near 70 he is riskier, but he beats that price per game if he plays 60 games.
In one expert auction mock he went for 20 USD, more than Franz Wagner or Jaren Jackson.
Josh would pay up to 11 USD for him at auction.
Memphis has a maxed 4-4-4 schedule in our playoff weeks through March 28. It has only 13 back-to-backs, possibly the fewest in the league.
Experts expect Memphis to be a below-average team, but not to tank this season because of the new tanking rules.

durable.text: He was healthy at Purdue and played 66 games as a rookie. He then had foot surgery and a second surgery after returning for 11 games. That makes three significant ankle or foot problems in his first two seasons.
Health is the big concern. The repeated ankle injury moves him toward Kawhi and Embiid territory, but he is not there yet.
He gives an elite FG% on solid volume, plus strong rebounds and blocks.
He is a very good free throw shooter for a center, so his FT% does not hurt a team.
He is poor in assists, threes and steals, and his turnovers are high for a center.
He can handle high usage. In a small sample he was one of the most efficient and dominant players in the NBA, and he turned 50% of his rim contests into blocks.

note: Edey went for just 2 USD in our league last season. Yahoo values him at 15 USD (rank 71) but its average cost is only 5 USD, and ESPN has him at 2 USD (rank 114). Experts take him around picks 60 to 70, and their auction bids run from Josh's 11 USD cap up to 20 USD, so somewhere between 10 and 15 USD gets you real upside for the injury risk. He fits builds that want FG%, rebounds and blocks and can live without threes, assists and turnovers. He also has a strong 4-4-4 playoff schedule. In the first weeks, check whether his minutes go above the expected 25 to 28 and whether Memphis rests him on back-to-backs.
